title: Fullscreen target shared container — transform in-place, never reparent
trigger: Multiple UI pieces must stay visible together in fullscreen but the browser API fullscreens only one element, or a layout wrapper must arrange the fullscreen element's children.
principle: When sibling UI must stay visible in fullscreen, the fullscreen element must be their common ancestor, not the media element. Moving the fullscreen element itself (reparenting it into a wrapper) exits fullscreen — Chrome's top-layer detaches on DOM removal. Transform the fullscreen element IN-PLACE into a flex container and move its CHILDREN into a stage cell instead. If the fullscreen element is a replaced element (<video>) that can't host siblings, exit fullscreen and re-request on its parent container — better than fixed overlay because the parent can host real flex siblings.

cases.context: Player fullscreen button targets the video element — sibling subtitle panel disappears because it's outside the fullscreen layer
Split View wants to wrap the fullscreen player container in a flex row (video stage + CueList panel). Moving the fullscreen element into a new wrapper exits fullscreen.
Fullscreen element is a bare <video> (replaced element) that can't host rendered siblings — need fallback
cases.bad:
// Assume fullscreen element is always a container
fullscreenEl.appendChild(panel); // <video> can't render sibling divs → panel invisible

applyFor: Video players with side panels (subtitle, playlist, chat, annotations)
Media players where controls/overlays must stay beside the video in fullscreen
Content scripts that inject sibling UI into a site's native player
Any fullscreen transition where the browser API targets a child but a sibling must remain visible
Layout wrappers (Split View, Picture-in-Picture) that need to rearrange the fullscreen element's children
